title: Müller Grid — Swiss Academic Canon
description: A strict eight-column Swiss grid for the academic podium: flush-left Helvetica, a three-size type scale locked to the baseline, and a single red rule where ornament would otherwise creep in. Discipline made visible through alignment alone.
philosophy: This template treats the grid as argument and the typeface as voice — nothing earns its place unless it serves the logic of the content. It refuses decorative hierarchy, illustrative padding, and any size or weight outside the three prescribed cuts. Built for the presenter who believes a rigorous talk deserves an equally rigorous surface, and whose audience came to follow a proof, not to admire a theme.
goodFor: Theory-dense academic conference and symposium talks
avoidFor: Photo-led product launches or brand storytelling
Warm narrative pitches requiring visual warmth
Audiences expecting kinetic animation or visual entertainment
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide radiates the authority of a well-defended thesis: austere, unhurried, and completely sure of itself. A single vivid rule acts as the sole expressive gesture — a scalpel line that separates declaration from context, warmth withheld but precision offered. Composition is asymmetrically weighted toward the left, creating directional tension against the open negative space to the right. Avoid any softening flourish, decorative motif, or centered arrangement; the discipline of strict left-alignment and bare white field is the drama.

examples.layoutNotes: Eight-column Swiss grid; title occupies columns 1–7, flush-left, sitting in the upper-middle third of the slide. A single horizontal rule at full column-width bleeds from col 1 to col 8, positioned as a hard dividing line between the title block and the subtitle/deck-topic line beneath it. Subtitle and speaker/institution attribution stack flush-left in cols 1–5, two baseline units below the rule. Outer margin held at roughly 9% on all sides; no header band, no footer — only a small folio numeral anchored bottom-right at col 8.

examples.promptCore: Swiss academic severity — the slide should feel like a rigorous journal page projected at lectern scale, with no concession to visual warmth or decoration. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric but taut: a narrow stub column anchors the label or counter while the wider field to its right carries the argument, producing a deliberate left-to-right reading path from anchor to exposition. The single accent-colored rule is the only graphic gesture, functioning as a load-bearing structural divider rather than ornament. Avoid any rounded element, centered alignment, illustrative padding, or breathing space that would soften the forensic discipline of the layout.

examples.layoutNotes: Eight-column Swiss grid with an 8% outer margin on all sides; the slide's section label or running counter occupies column 1 as a flush-left stub, while body content spans columns 2–8. A single hairline rule in the accent color runs the full content width immediately beneath the stub label, acting as the sole structural divider. Body content — proof steps, flush-left bullets, or a block quotation with attribution — is locked to the baseline grid across exactly three size cuts: heading, body, and attribution/footnote. Page number sits flush-right at the bottom margin, outside the primary content columns and set in the smallest prescribed cut.
